label: L=9 copy step 2 (t=10, the step after <DEL>), sparse token-dependent subset
explanation: Very sparse (0.03% of steps). It fires almost only at one position: the step right after <DEL> in length-9 sequences (t=10, recall_idx=1, input = the first original token fed back, output = original token 1). That slot holds 99.4% of the activation mass. The other 0.6% is t=9 in L=8 sequences, the same slot one step earlier. It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter step, in later copy steps, or for L<=7. Precision is very low, though: it fires on only about 2% of L=9 sequences at that slot. Which ones it fires on depends on tokens, not cleanly. It is enriched when the first token is z, 1, 2 or q (z is 6x), when the output or next output is a digit, l or y, and when there are more digits overall (n_digits >= 3 gives about 4-10x). No simple token rule separated hits from misses: the best token-conjunction predicate tried reached only dev F1 0.28. Magnitude is tiny (max 0.015) and the strongest cases mostly start with z or 1.
